summary: Multi-tier pricing mismatch on split-region batch run causing provisional credit reversal
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an unexpected invoice increase after a large split-region batch embedding job completed on 2026-03-09. A provisional credit was issued automatically by billing but was subsequently rolled back, causing a spike on the provisional invoice and a customer alert.

Impact:
- Nimbus Media reports a +62% increase on their provisional line item for 2026-03-09 batch run compared to expected blended estimate.
- Affects production workloads for a customer on Dedicated reserved capacity. Billing alert triggered downstream financial reconciliations.

Timeline (customer-provided):
- 2026-03-09 02:10 UTC: Large batch job (multi-queue) submitted targeting us-east and eu-west.
- 2026-03-09 02:15-03:05 UTC: Batch execution; postbacks received.
- 2026-03-09 04:00 UTC: Provisional credit generated by hourly smoothing service.
- 2026-03-10 08:20 UTC: Credit reversed by automated postback-reconciler; customer invoice shows spike.

Expected behavior:
- Multi-region postbacks should be attributed to the correct regional pricing tier and reserved capacity discounts applied consistently. Provisional credits should not be reversed without manual review when the reversal materially affects invoice totals.

Requested outcome:
- Clear explanation of why the provisional credit was reversed and restoration of the credit if reversal was erroneous. Permanent fix or mitigation to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On a dedicated org with reserved capacity in multiple regions, submit a multi-queue batch embed job that fans out to us-east and eu-west.
2) Allow job to complete so that postbacks trigger hourly smoothing and provisional credit logic.
3) Observe billing provisional line item and any automated reversals in billing audit logs and postback reconciler events.

investigation_notes:
Initial findings: automated logs show that microbatch 18 arrived at the postback-processor with an empty region_tag; previous entries for same job included explicit region tags. Hypothesis: scheduler change (multi-queue fanout optimization deployed 2026-03-08) introduced a path that omits region metadata for late-fanout microbatches, causing the postback-reconciler to classify them as 'unclassified' and trigger fallback pricing logic. That fallback selected a higher public-hosted rate instead of the dedicated reserved tier for the affected tokens, leading smoothing to apply then reverse when reconciliation detected inconsistent attribution.
Supporting evidence: billing audit events reference credit reversal reason \"region_tag_mismatch\" and reconciler trace IDs point to postback-processor runs created after the 2026-03-08 scheduler deploy. Dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/billing/postback-audit?org=nimbus (investigation view); relevant reconciler trace: trace.redwood.ai/trace/84b7c9f2.
Next steps taken: alerted infra team and rolled a temporary guard to reject postbacks with empty region_tag to avoid auto-reversal loop. Requested a full postback consumer replay for the job to re-run attribution and re-evaluate credits.

2026-03-10 15:30 UTC - Billing Ops (Elena Morales): Reversal was automated due to reconciler rule R-215 which marks un-tagged postbacks as misattributed. We put a temporary hold on automatic reversals for Nimbus org while SRE investigates; hold ID=HOLD-2042.

2026-03-11 08:47 UTC - Nimbus billing contact (Jordan Lee): Thanks — can you confirm whether the reinstated credit will appear on the finalized invoice or requires manual adjustment? Our accounting needs clear artifact for audit.

2026-03-11 10:05 UTC - Marco Nguyen (SRE): Replayed postbacks completed; attribution corrected for microbatch 18. Billing ops notified to re-evaluate reversal. Pending manual reissue of credit and a confirmation once posted to invoice.

2026-03-13 16:20 UTC - Elena Morales (Billing Ops): Provisional credit reissued as credit_id=pc-88412-R1 for amount_usd=+352.40. Customer will see adjustment in next interim billing refresh. We will update this ticket when the invoice line is reconciled.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: temporary guard to reject empty region_tag postbacks and a postback replay was executed for the impacted job; billing ops reissued the provisional credit pending invoice reconciliation. Root cause: a scheduler fanout optimization omitted region metadata for late microbatches under certain path conditions. Fix: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/1893 reintroduces explicit region tagging for all fanout branches and includes unit tests. Postmortem and permanent fix scheduled with SRE and Billing teams. Follow-ups: (1) CONF-# for postmortem to be published, (2) retrospective on reconciler rule R-215 to reduce auto-reversals without manual review for material credits, (3) customer-facing invoice artifact to be delivered to Nimbus accounting.
